newsitem.title: USA: Latam needs improved air cargo facilities.
newsitem.headline: Latam needs improved air cargo facilities.

text.p: With explosive growth projected in Latin American cargo traffic, airports in the region must improve cargo handling and facilities, a top Miami International Airport (MIA) official said Wednesday.
"You've got to build big, simple cargo facilities," Peter Reaveley, manager of route development, told the Miami Conference on the Caribbean and Latin America.
The cargo warehouses need to be able to accommodate Boeing 747 main deck pallets, which are 26 feet high. The column pacing needs to be adequate to accommodate the huge cargo pallets, Reaveley said.
The warehouses should have lots of refrigeration space, he added, since most air exports from South America are perishable products such as fish, fruits and vegetables.

Local customs authorities need to work to speed clearance. "Right now 63 percent of the cargo that comes through Miami is paperless, and that will go up to 75 percent next summer. If we can do it, you can do it," Reaveley said.
"Good security is also a must," Reaveley said. "It is terribly important that inbound cargo go straight to the guy that paid for it."

Although many airports in the U.S. States and Latin America worry about drugs, Reaveley pointed out that a kilo of cocaine is worth about $8,000 on the street, but a kilo of I.B.M. "mother boards" is worth about $80,000, making anti-theft efforts essential.
Miami International, which is or will soon become the largest international cargo airport in the world, expects 1.7 million tons of international cargo to pass through MIA next year Reaveley said.
To acommodate that growth, MIA is spending about $1 million a week, or about $500 million total, to improve cargo buildings and systems. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
